rows.note: Use 正 as the casual all-purpose evaluation for an excellent performance or a great person or thing.

example.jyutping: ni1 coeng4 jin2 coeng3 wui2 zan1 hai6 zing3

rows.note: Choose 叻 when brilliant means especially intelligent, capable, or talented.

example.english: They’re brilliant—they can fix their own computer at such a young age.
example.traditional: 佢咁細個就識自己整電腦，真係叻。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gam3 sai3 go3 zau6 sik1 zi6 gei2 zing2 din6 nou5 zan1 hai6 lek1

rows.note: Use 光 for something that is visibly shining or giving off a lot of light.

example.english: The lamp is so brilliant that I can’t see the TV clearly.
example.traditional: 枱上盞燈咁光，我睇唔清電視。
example.jyutping: toi4 soeng6 zaan2 dang1 gam3 gwong1 ngo5 tai2 m4 cing1 din6 si6

rows.note: Use 鮮艷 for a colour that is both vivid and strongly saturated.

example.english: The colour of this dress is brilliant, so it will look great in photos.
example.traditional: 呢條裙嘅顏色好鮮艷，影相一定靚。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 kwan4 ge3 ngaan4 sik1 hou2 sin1 jim6 jing2 soeng2 jat1 ding6 leng3
